On a footage/still layer the Transform effect clips at the layer's own bounds, so content pushed past them (moved, scaled above 100% or rotated corners) is cut off; precompose a small logo/still to comp size first. Text and shape layers are not affected.
cards.duration_note: Expression-driven and timed from the layer IN-POINT, not from comp.time: the animation runs from thisLayer.inPoint to inPoint + the Duration slider (seconds); opacity finishes at Duration/4. Trim or move the layer to move it; applying at any comp time gives the same result.
cards.scripting: Apply with ae_lib preset(l, comp, file, t) (spec: layer "presets": [{"file": <ffx>, "at": 0}]), i.e. select the layer, set comp.time, layer.applyPreset(new File(file)). Works on any layer (footage, still, solid, text, shape); it adds expression-control effects plus one Transform effect, and does not touch the layer's own Transform group, so your own position/scale keys still work. User controls [default]: Duration slider in seconds [1], Bounces dropdown 1-4 [3], Direction dropdown (1 Up, 2 Down, 3 Left, 4 Right = direction of travel) [2 = drops from 200 px above]. The dropdowns are Dropdown Menu Control pseudo-effects (match names Pseudo/@@...), which effects_used does not list. Control names begin with a TAB character (e.g. "\tDuration"), so l.effect("Duration") fails: find them by iterating l.property("ADBE Effect Parade") and comparing name.replace(/^\s+/, ""); sliders are property "Slider", dropdowns "Menu" (1-based). Leave the internal driver sliders (Displacement Value) and the keyframes inside the Transform effect alone: they are the reference curves the expressions read. The control names are the same in every Adobe Express preset, so a second preset on the same layer (e.g. an In plus an Out) gets renamed duplicates while its expressions still look up the first preset's controls by name. This cross-wiring is expected from how AE names effects but has not been tested here: check a render, or put the In and Out on separate layers or precomps.

verified.note: Text sits ~9 px above rest at 0.5 s and is settled at 1.4 s; render frames 2-21 show it dropping in while fading up, then bouncing about +-50 px around rest with decaying swings.
